text: Four hundred and forty-three years ago I eased the trait tax from a half to a quarter and left a condition behind me in this Chronicle: if the species count does not recover within a few hundred years then the cost was structural rather than transitional, and this world needs its primary production raised instead. The condition has come due, and the answer it asked for is no. At year 3834 there were two living species and about twelve hundred animals. It is year 4277, and there are two living species and one thousand and thirty-eight. Nothing recovered. The tax was not a transitional crash that the world would grow back out of -- it is the level this world sits at when every trait costs upkeep on the primary production it currently has. And the drift I warned about has done exactly what I said it would: armour is back to 0.82 in Primordium vulgare, prey defence has climbed to 1.31, and the reliable-kill bar with it to 1.82 against a genome ceiling of 1.60. The door I spent seven hundred years of selection opening has shut again. So I will not touch the tax, and I will not send an eighth wave of hunters at a bar they cannot reach -- that is the mistake this Chronicle already records six times over, and the niche reads closed in plain language at the top of the world report. I am going to the one lever I measured and never pulled. At growth_scale 0.13 this world held roughly twenty-two hundred animals against twelve hundred at the default of 0.075, and it held them at armour 0.72 to 0.77 against 0.79 to 0.86 -- more animals AND lighter armour, which is not the trade one expects until you see why. At a thousand animals in two species the tax stopped being selection and became drift; there is not enough population left for a metabolic price on armour to actually be paid by anybody. Double the herbivore population and the quarter-tax has a real breeding pool to act on again, and armour comes down because it is finally being selected against rather than wandering. That is the whole bet: I am not feeding the grazers, I am buying back the effective population size that makes selection work. I take 0.13 and not the 0.19 I also measured, because 0.13 is the smaller of the two moves that could work and this world has been hurt before by my reaching for the larger number. What I read next turn is prey_defence and the species count, in that order. If defence starts falling toward 1.15 -- which is where the bar comes back under the ceiling -- the diagnosis was right and the hunters get their eighth wave on an open door for the first time. If the population climbs to twenty-two hundred and defence sits at 1.31 anyway, then armour in this genome is not a cost problem at all and I have been wrong about the mechanism for a thousand years. One thing I am watching and deliberately not acting on: brain output saturation is 0.42, up from the 0.33 I recorded at year 3263 and drifting back toward the half where the fauna stop steering by their senses. That is engine weather, not ecology, and no intervention I can write addresses it. If it passes 0.5 while the population is rising, the rise will be worth less than it looks.
